newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SKB bank seeks foreign listing-agency.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SKB bank seeks foreign listing-agency.

text.p: Slovenia's SKB Banka, the country's number two bank, is seeking a listing on a foreign bourse, Slovenian news agency STA reported on Thursday.
STA, quoting an SKB statement, said the bank had approached Nomura International and the Bank of New York to act as advisors in its bid for the listing.
SKB declined to make any immediate comment to Reuters. Traders said the listing would most probably be on the London Stock Exchange.
Prior to a listing, the plan would have to be approved by the banks' shareholders at a meeting scheduled for November 14, STA reported.

The bank also had to acquire the permission of the central bank, the Bank of Slovenia, to increase the current maximum holding by foreign shareholders from 30 percent to 49 percent, the news agency said.
Bank officials were quoted as saying SKB had decided to seek a foreign listing to increase the price of the bank's shares.
SKB shares have risen sharply in recent weeks on rumours of a pending foreign listing. The stock has soared 45 percent since the end of September, closing at 43,630 tolars on Thursday.
Sources close to the bank told Reuters it was unlikely the foreign listing would start before the beginning of 1997. -- Ljubljana newsroom, +386-61-125 8439
